routes.finding: Four separately attributed voices identify al-As ibn Wa'il; the compressed list is not one chain.
Ibn Ishaq through Yazid ibn Ruman preserves the al-As occasion narrative.
Al-Tabari expands Ibn Kathir's abbreviated Shamir ibn Atiyya attribution naming Uqba ibn Abi Muayt.
Ikrima and Ibn Abbas are preserved as separate voice routes, not one combined chain.
Al-Tabari confirms the lower chain but does not replace the unresolved direct al-Bazzar witness.
Ata's Abu Lahab alternative is retained separately and traced at index level to Ibn Abi Hatim.
Ibn Abbas's Abu Jahl attribution is traced through al-Suyuti's four-source cluster and kept separate from adjacent Ibn Abbas reports.
unresolved: four direct source editions and chains

cross_route_decisions: All seven extracted routes remain separate evidence routes.
No compressed attribution list is converted into a single isnad.
Same-report-family parallels do not replace unresolved direct source locators.
Ibn Kathir's reported sahih judgment for 108-I09-R02 is not independently adopted.
The Abu Lahab and Abu Jahl alternatives remain distinct from the al-As ibn Wa'il reports and from each other.
The chronologically rejected expanded Abu Jahl/Ibrahim narrative is excluded from the bare 108-I10-R02 attribution.
Arabic remains controlling wherever the English entry omits voices, referents, chains, or narrative detail.
explicit_absences: No route in this consolidation receives a new authentication ruling.
No unresolved direct edition, report number, page, narrator variant, or chain is silently completed.
No new interpretive proposition is added.
This consolidation does not mark Ibn Kathir or Surah 108 complete.
next_step: Re-audit the complete Ibn Kathir route inventory and remaining non-route claim boundaries before any scholar-completion decision.
